subject: Proposal: weekend response schedule and escalation plan for Memorial weekend
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: ops-oncall@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: weekend response schedule and escalation plan for Memorial weekend

Team —

Quick background: we have two constraints for the upcoming Memorial weekend (Sat-Sun): a) a number of engineers are on PTO and b) our junior on-call cohort is still ramping after the new rotation change. We expect the normal P1 coverage to be stretched between 00:00–08:00 PT.

Ask: I want to propose a temporary, narrowly scoped adjustment to our P1 response expectations for that weekend to reduce risk of noisy escalations that we cannot properly triage overnight. Proposed changes (effective 2027-05-29 00:00 PT through 2027-05-31 08:00 PT):
- P1 acknowledged response target: extend from 60 minutes to 120 minutes for midnight—08:00 PT window only.
- P2 unchanged (4 hours).
- Required compensating controls:
  - Auto-fallback: any P1 not acknowledged within 90 minutes triggers an automatic page to the Dedicated account manager and the on-call engineer escalation path (PagerDuty escalation policy "Weekend Urgent").
  - For customers in our top-25 ARR tier, we will open a temporary dedicated channel (Ops Slack) and proactively outreach within 30 minutes of any P1 incident creation.
  - Post-weekend RCA and a one-off credit (TBD by Sales) for any customer with an incident that violated the normal SLA window.

Attachments: I attached a draft customer notice and the updated weekend escalation runbook for review.

Why this direction: It’s preferable to set an explicit, communicated expectation for a short window rather than leave customers guessing or escalate to C-levels later. This is time-boxed (one weekend) and paired with stronger escalation automation.

Please reply with: (1) objections, (2) alternate coverage ideas, and (3) recommended credit thresholds if a P1 actually breaches the classic 60-minute target.

Thanks —
Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Head of Support Operations | Redwood Inference
E: evelyn_hart@redwood.com | M: +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: draft-customer-notice-memorial-weekend.pdf (PDF, 14KB), weekend-escalation-runbook-v2.md (text, 8KB)

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, ops-oncall@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: weekend response schedule and escalation plan for Memorial weekend

Evelyn —

Appreciate the clear mitigation list. My immediate thought is to avoid changing customer-facing SLAs if we can staff to meet them, but I acknowledge the headcount cliff for this weekend. Two suggestions:

1) Partial manual cover: rotate one senior Support Engineer to the overnight slot (00:00–04:00 PT) for both Sat and Sun. That would reduce the extended-window to 04:00–08:00 (so effectively P1 extension only 04:00–08:00). We can pay the on-call premium for those shifts from the incident budget.

2) Keep your auto-fallback but tighten the trigger: page Dedicated AM at 75 minutes, PD escalation at 90 minutes.

If leadership wants to avoid manual rotas, your original plan is acceptable given the compensations. I’ll run a quick availability check with the senior cohort and confirm by EOD. Either way we should keep the customer notice conservative (explicit that it’s a limited change and that we have active escalation).

—Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Director, Support Engineering | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Accounts-Sales@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: weekend response schedule and escalation plan for Memorial weekend

Evelyn / team —

This makes sense from an operational point of view, and I agree we should prefer a communicated, time-boxed adjustment rather than surprise behavior. A couple of notes from Sales:

- Customer notice: keep language reassuring and specific. Offer a direct point of contact for top-tier customers and list the temporary hours where the extended window applies. I can edit the draft PDF and coordinate sends by Thu COB.
- Credits: for any verified P1 that exceeds the standard 60-minute SLA I recommend a sliding credit — 5% revenue for the week for customers under $25k ARR, 10% for $25k–$250k, and case-by-case for >$250k with AM approval. That should be enough to avoid churn while keeping our exposure manageable.
- Escalation phone numbers: confirm that the Dedicated AM on-call cell is included in the runbook; customers often ask for a single number to dial.

I’ll queue the draft notice edits and a short FAQ for AMs. If we go with Dylan’s partial manual cover plan, that reduces the likely credits needed.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Miles <jordan.miles@opify.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: support@opify.com, ops-esc@opify.com
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: weekend response schedule and escalation plan for Memorial weekend

Evelyn —

Thanks for the heads up and for including the runbook. A couple of quick clarifications from our side before we finalize:

1) Escalation contact: will the Dedicated AM cell be the single point of contact for top-tier customers? Please confirm the number you plan to list in the notice.
2) SLA scope: does the temporary P1 window extension apply to incidents caused by third-party cloud providers or only Redwood service degradations? Our contracts sometimes differentiate.
3) Credits: we appreciate the sliding scale proposed by Marissa; can you confirm whether the credit applies automatically or requires a claim?

We prefer the tighter window if you can staff it (Dylan’s suggestion). If not, we accept the limited temporary adjustment provided there is clear, proactive communication and the escalation contacts are reachable. Please loop me when the customer notice is finalized.

—Jordan Miles
Head of Ops, Opify
jordan.miles@opify.com
